section_70_scientific_editions.rule: German UrhG §70 protects editions of unprotected works/texts only where they result from scientifically organised activity and differ substantially from previously known editions; the related right expires 25 years after publication.
section_70_scientific_editions.application: The source used is the original 1819 edition, not a later scientific or critical edition. No new scholarly apparatus, commentary, or editorial apparatus from a modern edition is used. The modern digital transcription is only a cross-check; the Russian text was prepared directly from the 1819 source and the original scan pages.

section_71_posthumous_works.rule: German UrhG §71 provides a 25-year related right for a previously unreleased work first lawfully released after copyright expiry.
section_71_posthumous_works.application: Not applicable: this tale was published in the 1819 edition during the lifetimes of the named Brothers Grimm editors; it is not a previously unreleased posthumous work.

article_99_1_first_publication.rule: Polish Copyright and Related Rights Act, Article 99¹: 25-year exclusive right for a publisher who first lawfully publishes or otherwise disseminates a work whose copyright term has expired and whose copies were not previously made publicly available.
article_99_1_first_publication.application: Not applicable: the tale was first published in 1819 while its named editors were alive and their copyright was still running. This is not a first post-expiry publication.

article_99_2_critical_or_scientific_edit.rule: Polish Copyright and Related Rights Act, Article 99²: 30-year related right for a critical or scientific edition prepared after the copyright term has expired.
article_99_2_critical_or_scientific_edit.application: Not applicable: BookCheef uses the historical 1819 source edition and its PDM scans for verification, not a later critical or scientific edition. No critical apparatus or modern scholarly editorial content is reproduced.

article_36_and_39.rule: Article 36(1) sets 70 years from the death of the last surviving co-author; Article 39 counts full years following the year of the triggering event.
article_36_and_39.application: With the conservative last-survivor date of 20 September 1863, the term expired after 31 December 1933.

eu_eea.rule: Directive 2006/116/EC Article 1(1)–(2) sets life plus 70 years and uses the death of the last surviving author for joint works; Article 4 addresses first lawful publication of previously unpublished works after expiry.
eu_eea.application: The tale was already lawfully published in 1819 during the named editors' lifetimes. No post-expiry first-publication right is being relied on or reproduced.
